rule: Every resolved place remains selectable with its canonical score; only independently worthwhile settlements scoring 60 or more appear as town markers. Attractions never inflate settlement scores.
namingDecisions: The leading tilde is removed from Birse.
Kincardine o'neil is normalised to Kincardine O'Neil and kept distinct from Kincardine-on-Forth.
Marywell resolves to the AB34 Birse settlement and is kept distinct from Marywell near Portlethen.
Perde is corrected to the recorded Birse locality Percie.

additions.rationale: The village is assessed independently. Muir of Dinnet National Nature Reserve and surrounding estates belong in See coverage and do not automatically promote Dinnet above 60.
Glen Tanar House is retained in the selector as a named place. The wider estate, reserve, walks and event venue are separate visitor propositions and do not create a town rating.
Aboyne is likely to qualify after a complete attractions, trails, café, facilities and dated-heritage audit; the catalogue addition does not guess a 60+ result.
Birsemore Hill, Aboyne and the wider Birse landscape remain separately assessed; nearby scenery is not transferred into the locality score.
The leading tilde is removed from the requested name. Parish heritage and the Forest of Birse are retained as separate evidence rather than used to overstate the hamlet.
This is distinct from Kincardine-on-Forth. A complete audit must verify its own attractions, trails, cafés, parking, picnic provision, toilets and dated heritage before 60+ publication.
This is the AB34 Marywell in Birse, distinct from the existing Marywell near Portlethen. Nearby Finzean, Birse and Ballogie features are not borrowed into its score.
Finzean may qualify after a full audit of its own trails, cafés, practical facilities, attractions and dated heritage. Estate and wider landscape interest do not justify guessed publication.
The requested spelling is resolved to Percie using Birse parish and gazetteer evidence. Surrounding Finzean and Forest of Birse interest is not transferred to it.
Birse Castle, scheduled archaeology, hill routes and the Forest of Birse belong in See or trail coverage. They do not turn the locality itself into a 60+ town.
